messages:
ravi: opened a quick thread to capture the heuristic two-phase demote probe we talked about in the arch sync. sharing notes and owners.
sophia: thanks. goal is to avoid full cross-node leases while preventing stale routing after demote, right?
ravi: exactly. idea is two-phase: phase A = soft-mark publish + lightweight checksum, phase B = finalize demote after either local materialize or timeout/quorum. crucially routers use the checksum + gen to decide preference.
anya: how is checksum used? do readers need to fetch storage on mismatch?
ravi: checksum is a cheap in-memory hint published with the marker. readers validating a token can compare checksum; if mismatch they either hit local tombstone cache or fall back to authoritative read. checksum avoids a remote read in many cases.
tle: what about checksum collisions causing false fallbacks?
kevin: choose a 64-bit FarmHash or SipHash over tombstone digest; collision risk negligible for our workload. still instrument collisions and degrade to full verify if suspicious.
sophia: routing behavior: when a demote marker with gen G arrives we set ephemeral affinity to publishing node for TTL T. routers prefer that node for reads with gen < G, but readers still validate gen and fallback to read-through on mismatch.
anya: affinity TTL needs tuning. too long and you risk load skew; too short and you get misroutes. propose starting T=150ms with adaptive extension when read-through QPS rises for that prefix.
tle: adaptive extension: if fallback rate for prefix > threshold then extend TTL up to max 1s and signal publisher to speed up materialize ops. also add a backoff to avoid oscillation.
kevin: owners and immediate experiment plan?
ravi: owners: i will implement marker publisher + checksum emitter behind FF; tle will add chaos harness tests simulating delayed materialize and mixed-version clusters; anya will own telemetry/dashboards and runbook updates; sophia will prototype router affinity logic. aim: land staging FF in next 48h and run a 72h canary at 10% traffic.
anya: telemetry: demote.marker_published, demote.checksum_mismatch, demote.gen_mismatch_fallback, demote.affinity_extension_count, read_through.latency and qps per-prefix. add alert if fallback rate > 0.2% sustained.
tle: tests: deterministic harness that stalls materialize on one replica, fires demote then concurrent reads; assert no 5xxs, exactly one fallback per mismatched request and affinity TTL behaves monotically. also fuzz harness for checksum collision find.
sophia: corner cases: partition where publisher never completes phase B. we must ensure TTL expiry causes routers to stop preferring publisher; after TTL reads should default to read-through. also ensure we don't deadlock on repeated demotes - add a demote cooldown per-prefix.
kevin: rollout safety: feature-flag, kill-switch to disable affinity, canary with traffic shaping to monitor read-through RPS and percentiles. document rollback steps in runbook.
ravi: snippet of publisher and reader pseudocode: 
```
// publisher (phase A)
prefix.gen += 1
marker = { gen: prefix.gen, checksum: tombstone_digest(prefix) }
publish(marker)
// reader validation
if req.token.gen < marker.gen and marker.checksum != digest(req.cache_view):
  metrics.inc("demote.checksum_mismatch")
  return read_through(req)
else
  serve_from_cache()
```
anya: minor ops ask: include trace tag demote.phase=A/B and node id of publisher so SRE can trace misroutes.
tle: agree. will wire tracing and ensure router emits a single fallback event per request.
sophia: long-term decision doc: compare this two-phase heuristic + checksum vs router-handshake vs stronger demote durability. include cost model for extra read-through QPS and tail latency impact.
kevin: good. please keep the short fix minimal and reversible. we want to measure cost before committing to bigger changes.
deploy-bot: feature flag ff/evict/two-phase-demote created and scheduled for rollout to staging.
ravi: thanks everyone. will post PR links and canary dashboard once available.
